task_name: Wharfside Folk Festival - Restored festival identity
client_brief:
Bring our painted festival wordmark into a usable anniversary kit

Wharfside Folk Festival is twenty years old. The shed-painted wordmark is part of that history, and we want to retain its character across the handbill, cloth and supporting anniversary materials.

What we need back
- Recovered festival mark: 1 named export. The source lettering is preserved.
- Festival poster: 1 named export. The billing order follows the approved lineup. The event date is readable.
- Festival handbill: 1 named export. The venue details are readable at print size. The ticket action is visible.
- Festival shirt artwork: 1 named export. The ink limits follow the supplier note. The mark remains recognisable on the garment.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Independent three night folk music festival producing a screen printed poster programme and act cards for its twentieth year.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2006, on the working harbour at Fairhaven, Maine, a three night festival printed by a two person hand screen shop two streets away.
brand_identity.about: Wharfside is a three night folk festival on the working harbour at Fairhaven, in its twentieth year. Everything it prints comes off a two person hand screen shop that has printed the festival since the beginning, on a press that runs four inks plus the colour of the paper. The visible, hand pulled look is the festival's signature, and people frame the posters every year.
brand_identity.audience: Festival goers and locals at thirty five to sixty dollar tickets, many of whom already own the last five years of posters and buy the new one as a twenty dollar framed keepsake.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Community festival pricing, tickets thirty five to sixty dollars and posters sold afterwards at twenty dollars. The slightly imperfect hand pulled screen look is the value, not a corner cut.
brand_identity.typography: Wharfside sets three faces it already owns. Step 01 is Sentinel Black caps at 96 pt on 82.5 pt with tracking at -10 units, that leading being 0.86 of the size so the two lines nearly touch, and every act name breaks across exactly two lines however short it is, over a 4 pt Rust Red rule; the same setting runs at 40 pt on 34.5 pt for shirt art. Step 02 is the supporting bill in Trade Gothic Bold Condensed No. 20 at 34 pt on 36 pt with tracking at +10 units, always on a single line. Step 03 is venue, date and ticket copy in Adobe Caslon Pro Regular at 11 pt on 15 pt, tracking 0 units, measure held to a maximum of 65 characters, and step 04 is the handbill setting in the same face at 9 pt on 12.5 pt with tracking at +8 units. The wordmark is never set in Sentinel, and every one of these lines prints from the shop's four inks plus the colour of the kraft.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plainspoken, of the place. Example line: Three nights of folk on the old harbour, twenty years and counting.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists only as white paint on the weathered timber of the harbour shed, photographed from the quay, with no file and none ever made. The approved twentieth year illustration exists as a single flattened scan of a gouache and watercolour painting, no layers. The screen shop's own act card from last year is on file as the format.
brand_identity.values: Keeping the hand pulled, limited ink look that makes the posters worth framing, and staying continuous with nineteen years already hanging in local kitchens.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: Every headline act name is Sentinel Black caps at 96 pt broken across exactly two lines however short the name, leading pulled to 0.86 of the size so the lines nearly touch, over a 4 pt Rust Red rule.

scale.note: Caps. The slash in the sample marks the mandatory break: the line always splits across exactly two lines however short it is. Leading is 0.86 of the size, which is 82.5 pt at 96 pt, so the two lines nearly touch. A 4 pt Rust Red rule sits under the pair. Shirt art uses the same setting at 40 pt on 34.5 pt.

scale.sample: Three nights on the working harbour
scale.note: The supporting bill. Size already stated in the existing prose. Never broken across two lines, which is what keeps the two-line break readable as an act name.

scale.sample: Tickets thirty five to sixty dollars on the old harbour.
scale.note: Venue, date and ticket copy. Both numbers already stated in the existing prose.

scale.sample: Printed two streets away, four inks on kraft paper.
scale.note: The handbill setting. 9 pt comes from the existing prose; leading and the slight positive tracking are added so Caslon holds up small on uncoated kraft.

type_system.signature_move: Every headline act name is Sentinel Black caps at 96 pt broken across exactly two lines however short the name, leading pulled to 0.86 of the size, which is 82.5 pt, so the lines nearly touch, over a 4 pt Rust Red rule. Step 01 carries it, and step 02 is deliberately single line so the break stays the act name's alone.
rules: Never set the wordmark in Sentinel.
Every headline act name breaks across exactly two lines, however short the name.
Leading on step 01 stays at 0.86 of the size and is never opened up.
A 4 pt Rust Red rule sits beneath the two-line act name.
Shirt art is the same Sentinel Black caps setting at 40 pt, never another face.
The supporting bill stays on one line so the two-line break belongs only to act names.
All type prints from the four inks the hand screen shop runs plus the colour of the kraft paper. The hand pulled register is the look, not a fault to be corrected.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
